text: Representation translation refers to the cognitive process through which information encoded in a source representation is interpreted and reconstructed in a target representation ( Janvier, 1987 ). Subsequent research has emphasized that translation involves extracting relevant relationships from a source representation and re expressing those relationships in accordance with the conventions and constraints of a target representation ( Adu-Gyamfi et al., 2012 ; Keig and Rubba, 1993 ). Importantly, representational translation is conceptually distinct from representational recognition. Empirical studies demonstrate that recognizing a representation and translating it into another rely on different cognitive processes, with translation requiring deeper interpretive and constructive activity ( Campos et al., 2020 ; Lesh et al., 1987 ). Successful representational translation therefore depends on identifying which features of the source representation are conceptually essential and determining how those features map onto the representational grammar of the target format ( Ainsworth, 2006 ; van Heuvelen and Zou, 2001 ). This process imposes substantial cognitive demands, as learners must simultaneously interpret the source representation, suppress misleading surface features, and construct a coherent target representation, placing pressure on working memory and attentional control ( Adu-Gyamfi et al., 2017 ; Janvier, 1987 ).
